question:
The radius of a sphere is measured as $5$ cm with a possible error of $0.01$ cm. Estimate the maximum errors in calculating:
(a) its surface area,
(b) its volume.
explanation:
Given measurement
$$r=5\text{ cm},\qquad |dr|=0.01\text{ cm}$$
Error in surface area
The surface area is $S=4\pi r^2$. Hence,
$$dS=8\pi r\,dr$$
Therefore,
$$|dS|=8\pi(5)(0.01)=0.4\pi\text{ cm}^2$$
Error in volume
The volume is $V=\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3$. Hence,
$$dV=4\pi r^2dr$$
Therefore,
$$|dV|=4\pi(5)^2(0.01)=\pi\text{ cm}^3$$
Conclusion
The estimated maximum errors are $0.4\pi$ cm$^2$ in the surface area and $\pi$ cm$^3$ in the volume.
